text: Lucrative means making a lot of money. A lucrative job, business, or trade is one that pays off big. The secret ant trade is lucrative because a queen that costs about 3 dollars in Kenya sells for more than 200 dollars abroad.

Abundant means existing in large amounts, with plenty to go around. Kenya has abundant harvester ants, meaning huge numbers of them live there naturally. That is one big reason smugglers collect their ants there.

To forage is to move around searching for food, the way wild animals do. Squirrels forage for acorns; these ants forage for seeds and other food across the grasslands. As they forage they end up spreading grass seeds, which helps the whole savannah.

Something that makes your skin crawl gives you the creeps, like you can feel tiny things moving on you. It is a common English saying for feeling disgusted or creeped out. The writer is joking: this smuggling case involved thousands of live ants, so the crawling was almost real.

Smuggling is secretly moving things across a border when the law says you may not. A smuggler hides the goods, in suitcases for example, to sneak them past airport checks. Here the smugglers hid live ants in plastic tubes in their luggage.
Nairobi is the capital city of Kenya, a country in east Africa. Its international airport is one of the busiest in Africa, which is why officers there catch so many smugglers passing through.

A conviction is a court officially deciding that someone is guilty of a crime. It is not the everyday sense of a strong belief. The smuggler's conviction meant a judge found him guilty and sentenced him to a year in prison.

A craze is a sudden fashion that lots of people jump into at once, like a fidget-spinner craze at school. Crazes can fade as fast as they arrive. The craze here is keeping ants as pets, which spread around the world through social media.

The black market is all the buying and selling that happens illegally, in secret. It is not one place; it is the hidden trade in things that are banned or strictly controlled, like protected animals. Because sellers risk prison, black-market prices run far higher than legal ones.

Fuelled means fed something that makes it grow stronger or faster, the way fuel feeds a fire or an engine. It is the British spelling of fueled. The pet-ant craze fuelled the black market: more fans meant more buyers, which meant more smuggling.

A hub is the center a lot of activity flows through, like the middle of a bike wheel where all the spokes meet. An airport can be a hub for flights; a city can be a hub for music. Kenya has become a hub for the ant trade because so much of it runs through there.

To traffic something is to trade it illegally, usually moving it from place to place to sell. It has nothing to do with cars on a road. Traffickers are the people who run that illegal trade; Kenya's networks have long trafficked wildlife like ivory and pangolins.

A pastime is something you do for fun in your free time, a hobby that helps you pass the time. Reading, skateboarding, and video games are pastimes. Ant-keeping became a popular pastime during the pandemic, when people were stuck indoors.
An enthusiast is someone who is seriously into a hobby, a superfan. A soccer enthusiast watches every match; an ant enthusiast keeps whole colonies at home and watches them for hours.

A colony here is a group of ants that live together as one big family: one queen and thousands of workers in a shared nest. Bees and penguins live in colonies too. This is a different sense from a colony of settlers ruled by a faraway country.

A formicarium is a special see-through tank for keeping ants, like an aquarium but for an ant colony. The name comes from formica, the Latin word for ant. Owners watch the ants dig tunnels and build their miniature city inside it.

A phenomenon is something remarkable that happens and gets noticed, often something that grows surprisingly big. When the article calls ant-keeping a global phenomenon, it means the hobby exploded from a niche interest into something people do all over the world.

Prized means treasured and wanted, valued more highly than others. It is not about winning a prize. African harvester ants are especially prized by collectors because they are huge and live fascinating group lives.

t: the tigers of the ant world
text: This is the scientist's way of saying these ants are the big, impressive stars of their kind, the way tigers are the most awe-inspiring big cats. They are among the largest ants on Earth. Sadly, like tigers, being famous and impressive also makes them a target for illegal traders.
An entomologist is a scientist who studies insects: ants, bees, beetles, butterflies. The article quotes Dino Martins, an entomologist in Kenya, who studies how ants fit into the local environment.

Breeding means producing babies. The breeding female in an ant colony is the queen, the only ant that lays eggs. Every other ant in the colony hatched from her eggs, which is why losing the queen eventually ends the whole colony.

An ecosystem is a community of living things plus their home: the animals, plants, soil, and weather of a place, all depending on each other. Pull out one piece, like millions of ants, and the effects ripple to the grass, the soil, and the animals that eat the ants.

A savannah is a wide, grassy plain with only scattered trees, the classic African landscape where elephants, lions, and zebras live. East Africa's savannahs depend on healthy grass, and the article explains that ants quietly keep that grass growing.

To disperse things is to spread them out in many directions. A crowd disperses when everyone heads home. As ants carry grass seeds around, they disperse them across the savannah, planting the next generation of grass without meaning to.

A pangolin is a shy African and Asian mammal covered in hard scales, like a walking pinecone. It eats ants and termites with a long sticky tongue. Pangolins are themselves among the most trafficked animals on Earth, and fewer ants means less food for them.

Scrambling here means rushing frantically to deal with something, like scrambling to finish homework the morning it is due. Nothing to do with eggs. The authorities are scrambling because the ant trade grew faster than their ability to stop it.

An exodus is a mass departure, a huge number leaving a place at once. The word comes from the Bible story of the Israelites leaving Egypt. The illegal exodus here is thousands of ants being carried out of Kenya by smugglers.

The Kenya Wildlife Service is the government agency that protects Kenya's wild animals and runs its national parks. Its rangers and officers fight poaching and smuggling, and it is now pushing for tougher punishments for ant traffickers.
A seizure here is when officials take something away because it is illegal, like officers seizing the tubes of ants at the airport. This is the law-enforcement sense of the word, not the medical one.

This is a joke on the saying the tip of the iceberg, which means the small visible part of a much bigger hidden problem. Most of an iceberg, and most of an anthill, is hidden below the surface. The ants that get caught are probably a tiny fraction of the ants being smuggled.

Conservationists are people who work to protect nature: wild animals, plants, and the places they live. Conserve means to protect and keep from harm. The conservationists in this story warn that catching smugglers at the airport happens only after the ants have already been taken.
